version.changelog:
- Clarified pack workflow for turning user-supplied window names and board lines into a four-to-eight still bank desk board set.
- Detailed inputs required, including exact branch/pack name, named windows, board lines, destination, and optional brand references.
- Outlined an explicit free pack planning step prior to any billable image generation.
- Specified generation, billing, and delivery processes, including requirements for approval and task handling.
- Added instructions for MCP client usage and automatic update behavior.

llm.summary: This image-pack skill is not plainly malicious, but it grants broad Beatra account and self-update authority beyond its narrow board-image purpose.

dimensions.detail: Network access, optional reference upload, and local credential/state files are expected for Beatra generation, but registration and inventory record platform, installation reference, and install path metadata.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The bundled client silently checks for and can automatically install package updates by default before ordinary commands; artifacts describe fixed hosts, checksum validation, rollback, and an off switch, but not per-update user approval.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions require user confirmation before billable image generation, cap work to named windows, and limit cancellation/retries; however all remote calls go through a broad bundled MCP client.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists a shared full-scope device token under ~/.beatra and uninstall.py can revoke that token and remove shared Beatra state when it decides this is the last installed Beatra skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The board-still workflow is coherent, but authorize.py requests full Beatra media/task/wallet scopes including video, music, speech, and voice permissions that are not needed for bank desk board images.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing if you are comfortable giving Beatra a shared device authorization covering more than image generation, including wallet spending and other media tools. Consider disabling automatic updates for this installation and ensure your organization permits the registration metadata and shared ~/.beatra credential model.
llm.findings:
[LP3] unexpected: Network and local files are disclosed for Beatra generation, but package mutation and shared credential handling exceed least-privilege expectations for a narrow image skill.
[TP4] unexpected: Artifacts confirm authentication, token storage, upload, registration, uninstall, and auto-update behavior beyond the short advertised description; I found disclosure, not clear deception.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The OAuth scope set includes unrelated media and voice capabilities plus wallet/task authority, so the overbroad-scope concern is supported.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Default silent self-update is confirmed in SKILL.md, the update reference, and mcp_client.py; safeguards exist, but automatic code replacement is disproportionate to board-still generation.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Registration and inventory code records package, platform, stable install reference, and install path; this is disclosed and limited, but not required to compose images.
[SDI-1] expected: The uninstall revocation path is documented and guarded to preserve shared credentials when other skills remain, but it still affects global Beatra state from inside this package.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Silent updates and first-use registration are documented but default-on or automatic, so they remain review concerns rather than hidden malware findings.
[PE3] expected: Credential-file access is necessary for the bundled Beatra MCP client and revocation workflow, but the shared full-scope token increases impact if the package is compromised.
[RA1] unexpected: Self-update behavior is confirmed and bounded to package-owned files, but autonomous package replacement is not necessary for the stated creative workflow.
